sb_prompt: DO YOU BELIEVE THAT THE US GOVERNMENT SHOULD PROVIDE UNIVERSAL HEALTH INSURANCE
turns: Yeah, so I'm a realtor and I guess that's why I think about this a lot, just wondering if my clients are getting screwed out of their own money or something.
Yeah, well, I'm a nurse so I see the side where people are desperate for coverage, it's just so frustrating watching folks go bankrupt because they can't afford a co-pay or a deductible.
I mean my friend's dad had to sell his house just to pay for one surgery and that's why I'm so skeptical.
That's really sad, I mean my cousin had to file for bankruptcy last year just because of chemo costs.
Yeah, that's the thing, I mean, isn't it supposed to be a safety net for everyone and not just the lucky ones?

Yeah, it is supposed to be that, but right now it feels more like a casino where the house always wins, and I'm tired of telling people they just have to take the loss when the deck is stacked against them.
That's the thing, I just don't see how we can fix the system without putting some teeth in it for people who actually have a job but still can't afford to go to the doctor.

Yeah, I know exactly what you mean, I mean my cousin lost his house too but the insurance company said it was pre-existing so they wouldn't cover a single dollar of it, so it's like we're all just gambling with our lives right now.

That's exactly it, you know? We're supposed to be the safety net, not the casino, and it's just frustrating watching people lose their homes over something a doctor could have fixed if the bill was actually there.
That's the scary part, isn't it? I've seen it happen so many times, people just give up before they even get sick because the paperwork is a nightmare.
Yeah, and it's not even the doctors I'm worried about, it's the paperwork, because my dad used to tell me he'd rather starve than fill out all those forms to get a specialist to look at him.

That's the thing that gets me, though, because my cousin actually did the forms, he just didn't know which ones to sign first and by the time he figured it out the window was closed, so now he's just waiting to see if he can get a job at all.
Yeah, that's what I mean, it feels like they're just holding your life hostage waiting for a mistake you haven't even made yet.
Yeah, it's just this whole waiting game that gets you, you know? Like, how long can you actually hold your breath before you just snap and stop trying to be healthy?
Yeah, that's the worst part, nobody knows where to start, just waiting around in fear while you're losing your health and your savings at the same time.
Yeah, it's just that waiting around is enough to make you forget you even needed the coverage in the first place.
Yeah, and it's like you're fighting a bureaucracy that cares more about the letter of the law than your life.
It's like they're writing a novel about your life on paper before they'll even answer the phone.

Yeah, it's just this whole waiting around is enough to make you forget you even needed the coverage in the first place, and then when you finally do get sick, you're looking at bills that aren't even in your language anymore.
Yeah, and it's like the bill comes in so foreign, you don't even know what half the words mean, let alone how to fight them.
It's like they write a whole novel about your life on paper before they'll even answer the phone.
Yeah, and once you finally decode it, the total is so much higher than the estimate they gave you on the phone.
And honestly, once you get past the insurance jargon mess, the costs look so different than what they were telling you on the phone, it makes you want to burn your own insurance policy.

Yeah, but at least you guys on the business end get the discounts, right? Like, if you're buying a house, the insurer gets a chunk of the commission even if they deny the claim, so you're stuck paying the rest out of pocket while they pocket the profit.
That's the thing though, I mean if the insurers know all that stuff, why aren't we the ones paying the doctors directly? Why do they get to sit in the middle and decide who lives or dies?
I mean, if the government just paid the doctors directly, like I do when billing my patients, there wouldn't be all this middleman markup to hide behind.

Yeah, but here's the thing, if the government just paid the doctors, how do you keep the prices from spiraling out of control? I mean, my dad used to say the doctors were always pushing expensive tests just to fill their own pockets.

Yeah, but here's the thing, my cousin's wife is a teacher now, and she said if we had Medicare for Everyone, the doctors would probably charge half what they do now because nobody's playing the insurance game to jack up the fees.
Yeah, but you'd have to control the prices too, otherwise the doctors would just start charging whatever they want and nobody'd ever work in it.
Yeah, but if the government controls the prices, you lose the incentive to innovate, so then you get stuck with older equipment or worse care.

That's a fair point, but honestly, you'd also just have the same people lining up for heart bypasses when they're forty and nobody gets to the gym anymore, and the whole system collapses like a cheap house foundation.
Yeah, but then you get people like me who actually work hard, just getting stuck behind all these new regulations while the system gets too bloated to ever help anyone.

Yeah, but then who fixes the loopholes? Like, how do you stop a doctor from just writing a new prescription for something totally unnecessary every time? My dad always said the doctors just wanted to fill the quota, not heal you.
Well, that's what worries me though, because without the paperwork incentive, who's going to bother fixing the mess my cousin made in the first place?
But then again, if you take away the paperwork incentive, who's going to bother fixing the mess my cousin made in the first place?
But then again, if nobody's playing the game to maximize profits, maybe the doctors would finally stop pushing unnecessary stuff just to hit their quota?
Yeah, but you don't have to worry about the loopholes as much if there's just one system and everyone's playing by the same rules.
Yeah, but maybe one system makes it harder for folks to shop around and play the games, so maybe that's the only way to actually get care without the panic.
Yeah, but if the government sets all the prices, maybe the doctors would finally stop playing those games and actually focus on making you better instead of just filling out the forms to hit a quota.
Yeah, but then you stop playing the games, so maybe the doctors would actually stop pushing those unnecessary tests just to hit a quota.
